title: Trump Signs Psychedelics Executive Order: What It Means for Harm Reduction — and Why Some Are Still Left Behind
description: Trump's April 2026 executive order on psilocybin, MDMA, ibogaine, and LSD marks a quiet turning point for harm reduction in the US. But not every substance — and not every user — made it into the frame. Here's what clinicians need to understand.
author: SmokingTracker

title: Measurement-Based Care for Addiction: What It Is, Why It Works, and How to Actually Use It
description: Clinicians who rely on memory and in-session self-report are flying blind between appointments. Here's what the evidence says about MBC in addiction treatment — and how to actually implement it.
author: SmokingTracker

title: How Friction-Free Tracking Keeps Unmotivated Clients Engaged
description: Asking involuntary clients to 'just track' — without any pressure to change — is one of the most underused retention strategies in outpatient treatment. Here's why it works.
author: SmokingTracker

title: HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, and Client-Owned Addiction Data
description: Why giving clients full control over their substance use data isn't just legally required under HIPAA and Part 2 — it's clinically superior.
author: SmokingTracker

title: Nicotine and Cannabis: When You're Treating Two Addictions at Once
description: When a client rolls cannabis with tobacco, you're not treating one addiction — you're treating two. Most treatment plans only address one of them.
author: SmokingTracker

title: Cannabis and Sleep: Which Comes First?
description: Almost every cannabis client will tell you they need it to sleep. They're not wrong — and that's exactly the problem. A clinical breakdown of the sleep-cannabis dependency loop.
author: SmokingTracker

title: Cannabis Withdrawal Timeline: What to Tell Your Clients
description: Cannabis withdrawal is a recognized DSM-5 diagnosis with a predictable timeline. Here's what to expect week by week — and how to use that knowledge in treatment.
author: SmokingTracker

title: Signs of Cannabis Use Disorder vs. Casual Use: A Clinical Guide
description: Most clients will tell you they're casual users. The DSM-5 disagrees with at least some of them. Here's how to apply the criteria in a real clinical conversation.
author: SmokingTracker

title: Flower vs. Hash: What Counselors Should Know About Cannabis Forms
description: A deep dive into cannabis flower (bud), the difference between Indica and Sativa, and how different terpenes affect the client's experience.
author: SmokingTracker

title: Beyond THC: What Hash Color Tells You About a Client's High
description: Understand the connection between hash color, trichomes, and the chemical profile — and why dark hash often means a heavy, sedative experience for clients.
author: SmokingTracker
